content: The term left heart refers collectively to the left atrium and the left ventricle of the heart. In some contexts, it may also include the aorta, encompassing the left atrium, left ventricle, and aorta as a functional unit. The left atrium is responsible for receiving oxygen-rich blood from the pulmonary veins. This oxygenated blood is then directed through the mitral valve into the left ventricle. The left ventricle, in turn, pumps the blood through the aortic valve into the aorta, which distributes it to the rest of the body. The left side of the heart has a thicker muscular wall compared to the right side. This increased thickness is necessary to generate the higher pressure required to pump blood throughout the entire body, whereas the right side of the heart only needs to pump blood to the lungs.
